claims.claim: 7. How Label and PageLabel rows sync (tombstoned, delete-wins, last-writer-wins).

evidence.quote: /** §9.4 snapshot merge — a winning page record's label set fully replaces the local one. */

missed.fact: Label has a uid (unique index) but the uid never travels: labels sync by NAME only, inside the page record as a list of names. A label found by name locally, else created fresh with a new local uid and a colour derived from the name, so colour is not synced and the uid differs per device.
Label.color is derived from the name hash modulo an 8-colour palette (LabelColors.forName), and is never synced. Changing the palette size would recolour every label.

Label has no updatedAt or deletedAt, and no row-level sync record. It is the only identity in the page snapshot carried as a bare string. Two devices that create the same name concurrently converge through name lookup, but a name collision merges them.

The page's label set is whole-set replacement: a winning page record clears page_tags for the page and re-adds from names. Per-page last-writer-wins by page updatedAt, with no per-PageLabel merge and no PageLabel tombstone. A label removed on the losing side is lost.

Labels also bind to a PageDatabase (labelId, nullable) as its 'doorway': a page carrying the label becomes a database member, and with syncToTasks becomes a task. So a label applied to a page can create or trash a Task Entry (LabelMembership.applyLabel/removeLabel). The database's labelId has no FK, and its bound label travels by name as labelName.

Habit carries an optional single Label (labelId: Long?, no foreign key, used as the planner 'area'), which travels by name via labelNameOf/labelIdFor and groups habits by area. Because it has no FK, nothing blocks or cleans it.

Naming: entity Label maps to table 'tags', join PageLabel to 'page_tags' with column tagId, and the snapshot key is 'tags'. Renamed in name only (§0.6.9), so a grep for 'label' in SQL misses everything.

Label lookup is exact-match `name = :name` (SQLite default, case-sensitive for non-ASCII, case-sensitive for '=' on ASCII). Search uses LIKE, which is case-insensitive for ASCII. There is no unique index on name, so duplicates are possible at the DB level and only the create-on-type path in code prevents them.
The page filter uses OR semantics (any selected label), not AND.
Only PageLabel has a cascading FK to Label (onDelete CASCADE), but no code path deletes a Label, so the cascade is currently unreachable.
